messages.author: 0dd6c9694b3c4809
messages.subject: Organising the Reference manual file
parts:
One hassle with the file that Reference manual files  have (i.e., the list of all their functions, data etc), is that it is just an alphabetical dump, often burying the three key functions a nuser needs in dozens of randoms data set help functions, obscure non-user functions etc.

I am really enjoying the @family tag for functions, is there a way to use something like this to organize the reference manual?

Ideally a contents page made up of family-type tags, preferably with order control or even some hierarchy.

then the items with headings. So the user would see this:


Package Name
Intro paragraph. Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet, consectetur adipisicing elit, sed do eiusmod tempor incididunt ut labore et dolore magna aliqua. Ut enim ad minim veniam, quis nostrud exercitation ullamco laboris nisi ut aliquip ex ea commodo consequat. Duis aute irure dolor in reprehenderit in voluptate velit esse cillum dolore eu fugiat nulla pariatur. Excepteur sint occaecat cupidatat non proident, sunt in culpa qui officia deserunt mollit anim id est laborum.

Contents
1. core functions
2. plotting
3. miscellaneous
3 data sets
4. non-user functions

1 Core functions
# build()
# reparse()
# modify()

2 Plotting
# plot()
# forest()

3 Datasets
# merk
# esrc

4 Misc
# fix.it()
# abd()


Is that possible?

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Organising the Reference manual file
parts:
You could try using an INDEX
(http://cran.rstudio.com/doc/manuals/r-devel/R-exts.html#The-INDEX-file),
but I'm not sure if this is translated into the html help. Generally,
I think you're better off using vignette for this sort of
organisation.

Hadley

I guess I was looking for something automated - index has to be manually curated, and is ill-advised according to CRANny.

I think many people can't spell vignette :-) , and would love the ?packageName help to be just a little bit structured... A little would go a long way.

Best, t
